roleZh: 差分机与分析机的设计者 · 维吉尼亚密码的「失名英雄」
roleEn: Designer of the Analytical Engine · the unsung breaker of the Vigenère
bioZh: 查尔斯·巴贝奇是英国数学家与工程师。1830 年代他设计「分析机」，一台以打孔卡驱动的可编程机械计算机，被视为计算机思想的先驱。1854 年，他在破解维吉尼亚密码时发现了与卡西斯基检验法等价的方法：借助密文中重复片段的间距推算密钥长度。但因保密要求他从未发表，成果埋没于笔记，直到 1985 年才被学者重新发现——功劳早已记在九年后出版的卡西斯基名下。
bioEn: Charles Babbage was an English mathematician and engineer. In the 1830s he designed the Analytical Engine, a programmable mechanical computer driven by punched cards, and is regarded as a founding visionary of computing. Around 1854, while dabbling in ciphers, he broke the Vigenère cipher using a method equivalent to the Kasiski examination. Bound by a promise of secrecy, he never published, and the breakthrough lay buried in his notebooks until historians rediscovered it in 1985. By then, the credit had long since gone to Kasiski.
quoteZh: 「算术的全部，如今看来都可以交给机器。」
quoteEn: "The whole of arithmetic now appeared within the grasp of mechanism."
factZh: 冷知识：让巴贝奇出手的是一桩「发明权之争」——牙医思韦茨 1854 年宣称发明了新密码，巴贝奇一眼认出那是维吉尼亚密码并当场破解；这场笔战的手稿，成了他破译功绩的唯一证据。
factEn: Fun fact: Babbage tackled the Vigenère because of a priority dispute — in 1854 a dentist named J.H.B. Thwaites claimed to have invented a "new cipher." Babbage recognised it as the Vigenère and cracked it on the spot; the manuscripts of that exchange are the only record of his feat.

nameZh: 奥古斯特·克尔克霍夫斯
roleZh: Kerckhoffs 原则的提出者 · 现代密码设计的第一准则
roleEn: Author of Kerckhoffs' principle · the first rule of modern cipher design
bioZh: 奥古斯特·克尔克霍夫斯是荷兰语言学家与密码学家，大半生在法国教书。1883 年，他在法国《军事科学杂志》发表《军事密码学》，提出著名的「克尔克霍夫斯原则」：密码体制的安全性应完全依赖密钥保密，即便算法被对手彻底掌握也不应被攻破。这一原则日后成为现代密码设计的铁律，也是「算法公开、密钥保密」这一当代加密体系的思想源头。
bioEn: Auguste Kerckhoffs was a Dutch linguist and cryptographer who spent most of his career teaching in Paris. In 1883 he published "La cryptographie militaire," setting out six design desiderata for military ciphers. The second became famous as Kerckhoffs' principle: a cryptosystem must remain secure even if everything about it except the key falls into enemy hands. Modern cryptography treats this as a foundational rule — the reason today's standard algorithms such as AES are public, while only the keys stay secret.
quoteZh: 「体制不应要求保密，落入敌手也不应造成麻烦。」
quoteEn: "The system must not require secrecy; it must be able to fall into enemy hands without inconvenience."
factZh: 冷知识：克尔克霍夫斯的本职是语言学家，晚年积极推广人造语言「沃拉普克语」，还担任其官方学院的主持人；密码学只是他的副业，却留下了比主业更不朽的遗产。
factEn: Fun fact: Kerckhoffs' day job was linguistics — he was a leading champion of Volapük, a constructed international language, and directed its academy. Cryptography was a side project, yet it is the side project that made his name immortal.

roleZh: 多表替换密码的真正发明者 · 维吉尼亚密码的原作者
roleEn: True inventor of polyalphabetic substitution · the man behind the "Vigenère cipher"
bioZh: 焦万·巴蒂斯塔·贝拉索是意大利密码学家。1553 年，他发表《焦万·巴蒂斯塔·贝拉索先生的密码》，首次系统描述多表替换密码：以密钥词轮换字母表（即「塔布拉-雷克塔」），使同一明文字母在不同位置呈现不同密文，令频率分析失效。三十三年后维吉尼亚发表的方案核心正是贝拉索的设计——这套体制被后世冠以维吉尼亚之名，实为张冠李戴。
bioEn: Giovan Battista Bellaso was an Italian cryptologist from Brescia. In 1553 he published a treatise on ciphers that described, for the first time in print, polyalphabetic substitution: a keyword rotates through a series of alphabets — the tabula recta — so the same plaintext letter is enciphered differently at every position, defeating simple frequency analysis. Thirty-three years later Blaise de Vigenère published a cipher built squarely on Bellaso's core idea, and history attached Vigenère's name to it. The "Vigenère cipher" is, in truth, Bellaso's cipher.
quoteZh: 密钥词所至，字母表随之轮转——这便是多表密码的全部秘密。
quoteEn: Wherever the keyword goes, the alphabet turns with it — that is the whole secret of polyalphabetic ciphers.
factZh: 冷知识：贝拉索 1553 年的小册子还首创「互反字母表」——明文表与密文表互为倒序，加密与解密变成同一操作；这一便捷设计被后世众多密码沿用，而贝拉索本人的生卒年月却几乎失考。
factEn: Fun fact: Bellaso's 1553 booklet also introduced reciprocal alphabets — plaintext and ciphertext alphabets reversed against each other so enciphering and deciphering become the same operation. Yet almost nothing else about his life is known, not even his year of death.

roleZh: Enigma 转子密码机的发明者
roleEn: Inventor of the Enigma rotor cipher machine
bioZh: 阿图尔·谢尔比乌斯是德国电气工程师。1918 年，他申请了转子密码机的专利：可更换的转子组与插线板使字母替换的复杂度空前提高，并创办公司将其商品化，最初面向商业客户。1926 年起德国海军、陆军、空军相继列装，Enigma 成为二战德军的核心密码机。他 1929 年死于马车事故，没能看到自己的机器成为战争的主角。
bioEn: Arthur Scherbius was a German electrical engineer. In 1918 he patented a cipher machine built on rotors, and founded a company to sell it, first to the commercial market. From 1926 onward the German Navy, Army and Air Force adopted it in turn, and Enigma became the Wehrmacht's central cipher machine of the Second World War. Scherbius died in a carriage accident in 1929 and never lived to see his machine become the war's most famous cryptosystem.
quoteZh: 「Enigma」在德语里意为「谜」——他给机器起的名字，成了战争中最难解的谜题。
quoteEn: "Enigma" means "riddle" in German — the name he gave his machine became the hardest riddle of the war.
factZh: 冷知识：谢尔比乌斯的 Enigma 起初是卖给银行的商业产品，广告称其「保密性无可匹敌」；德军列装后，波兰密码局很快盯上了它——而发明人本人 1929 年就死于一场马车事故，年仅 50 岁。
factEn: Fun fact: Enigma was first marketed to banks as a commercial product with ads boasting "unrivalled secrecy." The German military adopted it in 1926; Polish cryptanalysts were studying it within years — while Scherbius himself died in a carriage accident in 1929 at fifty.

roleZh: 公钥密码的先驱 · Merkle 树发明人
roleEn: Pioneer of public-key cryptography · inventor of the Merkle tree
bioZh: 拉尔夫·默克尔是美国计算机科学家。1974 年，还是加州大学伯克利分校本科生的他提出「默克尔谜题」：双方通过公开信道交换海量谜题即可协商出共享密钥——这是史上第一个公钥密码构想，与迪菲-赫尔曼并列公钥密码学的开创者。他还发明了哈希树（Merkle 树），如今是区块链与分布式系统的核心数据结构。
bioEn: Ralph Merkle is an American computer scientist. In 1974, while still an undergraduate at Berkeley, he proposed "Merkle's puzzles": two parties exchange a large number of puzzles over a public channel and thereby agree on a shared secret — the first public-key scheme ever conceived, ranking him alongside Diffie and Hellman as a founder of public-key cryptography. He also invented the hash tree, universally known today as the Merkle tree, which underpins blockchains and countless distributed systems.
quoteZh: 在公开的世界里，也可以藏得住只有两个人知道的秘密。
quoteEn: Even in a public world, two people can share a secret no one else knows.
factZh: 冷知识：默克尔的「谜题」论文 1975 年曾被《美国计算机学会通讯》以「想法太过超前」退稿，直到 1978 年才发表——此时迪菲-赫尔曼的论文早已问世，公钥密码的功劳簿上，他只能与别人并列署名。
factEn: Fun fact: Merkle's puzzles paper was rejected by the Communications of the ACM in 1975 as "too far out" and only appeared in 1978 — by then Diffie–Hellman had already been published, so his place in history became a shared one.

roleZh: 秘密发明 RSA 等价算法的 GCHQ 数学家
roleEn: The GCHQ mathematician who secretly invented RSA
bioZh: 克利福德·科克斯是英国 GCHQ 的数学家。1973 年，年仅 23 岁的他在同事埃利斯「非秘密加密」构想的基础上，独立发明了与 RSA 等价的非对称加密算法——比公开的 RSA 早了整整四年。受英国《官方保密法》约束，这一成果从未发表，直到 1997 年才获准解密。此时 RSA 早已成为互联网加密的基石，他只能以「隐秘先驱」的身份被历史追认。
bioEn: Clifford Cocks is a British mathematician who spent his career at GCHQ. In 1973, aged just 23, building on James Ellis's concept of "non-secret encryption," he devised an asymmetric cryptosystem mathematically equivalent to RSA — a full four years before RSA was published. Bound by the Official Secrets Act, the work stayed classified until 1997. By then RSA had conquered the world; Cocks was recognised only in retrospect.
quoteZh: 我的工作不能署名，但数学本身会记住谁先到达。
quoteEn: My work could never carry my name, but mathematics itself remembers who arrived first.
factZh: 冷知识：科克斯的方案与 RSA 殊途同归——都建立在欧拉定理与因式分解的困难之上；但他的论文从未发表，直到 1997 年 GCHQ 解密，密码学界才发现「RSA 的原型」早已秘密存在了 24 年。
factEn: Fun fact: Cocks's scheme and RSA converged on the same mathematics — Euler's theorem and the difficulty of factoring. But his paper was never published; when GCHQ declassified it in 1997, the community discovered that a prototype of RSA had existed, in secret, for 24 years.

roleZh: 「非秘密加密」的提出者 · 公钥思想的隐秘先驱
roleEn: Proposer of "non-secret encryption" · the hidden pioneer of public-key cryptography
bioZh: 詹姆斯·埃利斯是英国 GCHQ 的密码学家。1969 年，他提出「非秘密加密」：加密与解密使用不同密钥，加密密钥可以公开，双方无需事先秘密交换——这正是公钥密码学的核心思想。他当时无法证明其可行性，便把问题交给同事；科克斯与威廉森据此先后发明了与 RSA、迪菲-赫尔曼等价的方案。这批成果因保密尘封近三十年，1997 年才解密公开。
bioEn: James Ellis was a British cryptographer at GCHQ. In 1969 he formulated the concept of "non-secret encryption": if encryption and decryption use different keys, the encryption key can be made public and two parties need no prior secret exchange — the essential idea of public-key cryptography. He could not prove it was possible, so he handed the problem to colleagues; Cocks and Williamson turned it into working schemes years ahead of the open literature. Classified for nearly three decades, Ellis's work was declassified only in 1997.
quoteZh: 我提出了一扇门，却打不开它——但门的存在本身，就是答案的一半。
quoteEn: I pointed at a door I could not open — but knowing the door exists was half the answer.
factZh: 冷知识：埃利斯 1987 年写下的内部回顾《非秘密加密的历史》如今是公钥密码隐秘史的第一手档案——解密后，学界称他为「公钥密码学被遗忘的祖父」；他 1997 年去世，几乎没等到这份迟到 28 年的承认。
factEn: Fun fact: Ellis's 1987 internal memoir, "The History of Non-Secret Encryption," is now the primary document of public-key cryptography's secret chapter — after declassification he was called "the forgotten grandfather of public-key cryptography." He died in 1997, just before the belated recognition arrived.

roleZh: Feistel 网络发明人 · DES 的核心设计者
roleEn: Inventor of the Feistel network · core designer of DES
bioZh: 霍斯特·费斯泰尔是德裔美国密码学家。他 1934 年移居美国，1960 年代加入 IBM 沃森研究中心，开始研究分组密码。他发明的 Feistel 网络把数据分成两半、经多轮函数混合，成为此后几乎所有分组密码的通用骨架；基于这一结构，他与团队设计出 Lucifer，并最终演化成美国国家标准 DES。在 AES 问世之前，DES 统治全球加密标准数十年。
bioEn: Horst Feistel was a German-born American cryptographer. He emigrated to the United States in 1934 and joined IBM's Watson Research Center in the 1960s, where he pioneered the field of block ciphers. His Feistel network — splitting data into two halves and mixing them through repeated rounds — became the universal skeleton of nearly every block cipher that followed. Building on it, he and his IBM colleagues created the Lucifer cipher, which evolved into DES, adopted as the U.S. federal encryption standard and used worldwide for decades until AES replaced it.
quoteZh: 把数据一分为二，让每一半都成为另一半的锁。
quoteEn: Split the data in two, and let each half be the other's lock.
factZh: 冷知识：IBM 团队最初的 Lucifer 使用 128 位密钥，而最终标准化的 DES 只有 56 位——外界长期怀疑是 NSA 在幕后要求削弱；这场「密钥之争」让 DES 带着后门疑云统治世界数十年，也开启了密码学界对政府标准的永恒争论。
factEn: Fun fact: IBM's original Lucifer used 128-bit keys, but the standardized DES kept only 56 — a cut widely suspected to have been demanded by the NSA. That suspicion shadowed DES for decades and opened the everlasting debate over government-designed standards.

roleZh: RSA 算法共同发明人 · MD5 哈希设计者
roleEn: Co-inventor of RSA · designer of the MD5 hash
bioZh: 罗纳德·李维斯特是美国密码学家、MIT 教授。1977 年，他与萨莫尔、阿德曼在 MIT 共同发明 RSA——世界上第一个实用的公钥密码体制，算法名中的「R」正是他的姓氏首字母；直到今天，RSA 仍是互联网加密与数字签名的基石。他还设计了 MD5 等哈希函数，参与创办 RSA Security 公司，2017 年与两位合作者同获图灵奖。
bioEn: Ronald Rivest is an American cryptographer and professor at MIT. In 1977, with Adi Shamir and Leonard Adleman, he invented RSA — the world's first practical public-key cryptosystem, whose "R" is the initial of his surname. It remains a cornerstone of encryption and digital signatures on the internet. Beyond RSA, he designed the MD5 and other widely used hash functions, co-founded RSA Security, and shared the 2017 Turing Award with his two co-inventors.
quoteZh: 两个大素数的乘积，就能守住全世界的秘密。
quoteEn: The product of two large primes can guard the secrets of the whole world.
factZh: 冷知识：传说 RSA 的灵感降临在 1977 年 4 月的一个夜晚——李维斯特在阿德曼家吃过逾越节晚餐后通宵工作，第二天清晨就把完整方案交给了两位合作者；「RSA」三个字母自此诞生，纯属按姓氏排列的巧合。
factEn: Fun fact: The legend goes that the RSA breakthrough came one night in April 1977 — after a Passover dinner at Adleman's home, Rivest worked through the night and handed his partners the complete scheme the next morning. The three letters, in alphabetical order by surname, were pure coincidence.
